item.title: Reanimating Elephant Graveyards
item.description: Every few decades an elephant graveyard reawakens, taking on humanoid forms
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Mostly the usual shtick, might include interview logs and/or discovery logs. This part isn't fleshed out yet and can still change a lot.

Elevator Pitch: All elephant graveyards are anomalous, the skeletons in them inevitably coming to live every 40-70 years. The living dead results reassemble themselves in a humanoid shape and move in a specific direction for 15 minutes before then falling apart again and repeating the process 40-70 years later.
The place they are moving towards is an obscure part of Russia where other elephant skeletons have already been stacked up many meters high in an intricate shape.
There also may be a secondary effect to the living skeletons that causes people to hallucinate, blurring the details of the encounter.

Central Narrative: No concrete narrative but rather the idea that the public is aware of the elephant skeletons, considering them an urban legend. The foundation would then have to base its procedures on that fact and make sure the people believe the scp to be a hoax.
The event's age would also be explored as parallels are drawn between it and cave drawings or alleged cyclops encounters.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main hook would be the vague knowledge that the public has of the scp, as well as the weirdness of the event itself. Similar ideas have been made into scps before but I believe that the specifics make my concept stand out among the others.

Additional Notes: The whole "humanoid elephant skeleton" idea is largely based on the theory that people used to mistake elephant skulls for those of cyclopes, creating that myth in the first place.
Specific numbers and values were mostly chosen to make the scp as annoying to contain as possible(a bit silly in hindsight).
I know that the idea still needs a good amount of polishing. I hope I can turn it into something sort of worthwhile in the end.

item.title: The Rube Effect
item.description: Woman evades death by a string of 'random' events that neutralizes immediate threats.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional, Comedy

Page Layout: Test and incident logs to be included. I intend to cross refence other works, but would like to ask permission from other authors before I commit to that.

Elevator Pitch: Woman is infected with a "virus" of sorts that neutralizes nearby deadly threats with 'events' that work on a similar principle to the butterfly effect or a Rube Goldberg machine. It can manipulate any non-organic material to complete an event. The woman is incredulously unaware of her anomalous properties.

Central Narrative: The virus is contagious but this is unknown by the Foundation at the time of the article's writing. Its effects are efficient but subtle. The Subject was the child of two researchers who were killed in a containment breach. She's sent to live at the School for Children of Prominence. A boarding school/orphanage for children of Foundation personnel. She is notably idiotic and it amazes her teachers that she actually graduates. Once she starts working for the Foundation as a junior researcher, her peers are dumbfounded that despite lacking all common sense she has yet to die. This prompts an investigation and her eventual classification as an SCP. After the article is submitted for review the higher ups begin to doubt the judgement of the lead researcher and try to have the SCP declassified due to 'lack or sufficient anomalous evidence'. The lead researcher is shunned and dives into a depressed drunken stupor. It remains to be seen if the Foundation will continue the research and discover how to harness the power of this virus.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The virus isn't all powerful and it wont infect just anyone. It's host can still be injured and it will not prevent death due to biological means such as old age or venom. It is, however, very good at keeping its host alive. The Foundation would kill to have something like this for all of their field agents.

item.title: Two Dimensional Love
item.description: Sounds good on paper, doesn't it?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch:

  • A bloodstained kirigami paper doll 1.56 meters in length drawn on to resemble a female human in an anime style, wearing gothic "lolita" style attire. Edges of the paper are abnormally sharp and capable of inflicting wounds on contact far greater than the amount of pressure and composition of the fibers would allow for. Subject is inanimate but believed to be sentient.
  • Any male who enters the doll's line of "sight" has an approximate 3% chance of being imprinted on, upon which its effect manifests. Upon entering REM sleep, the victim has a 50% chance to enter a state similar to sleep paralysis, in which a vision of the doll will appear to them and gently caress them, leaving deep wounds. This process is painless but can still result in complications from blood loss or infection.
  • Any female (biological or transgender) the victim interacts with that is not of blood relation enters a similar state the next time they sleep in which they are executed in a manner similar to the Chinese Lingchi. This process is not painless.
  • If the victim has not expired after a period of seven days, they will progress to Stage 2 in which they have an approximate 12.5% chance of the doll attempting to copulate with them. This normally results in death by blood loss. Only one affected victim can exist at a time.

Central Narrative: Article proceeds normally, with an addendum regarding its recovery from the belongings of a deceased Japanese man implied to be its creator after his "suicide" in police custody. Several experiment logs are listed near the end with the Foundation using D-Class to determine how it works.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Final experiment log has the Foundation manage to keep a D-Class alive long enough to describe Stage 2 to them. He explains that the doll, which was silent before then, kept repeating a single phrase: "Mō kakkoīdesu ka?" (Japanese for "Are we cool yet?")

item.title: My First SCP Idea: The Wooden Vulture
item.description: A "living" caved wooden vulture that eats human flesh
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes, but I don’t expect it’ll get greenlit at the first go. I’m mostly looking for feedback right now.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (optional): Unsure

Page Layout (optional): Contains containment procedures, description, discovery, test logs, and maybe even a cross-link.

Elevator Pitch: A “living” carved wooden vulture that feeds on human corpses. It will get “hungry” after 24 hours, which is when it will start searching for corpses to feed on. If it hasn't eaten for 36 to 48 hours, it will enter a frenzy, which makes it exponentially stronger and more aggressive. In this state, it will eat people alive in order to satiate its “hunger.” In this state, it will even ignore any dead human meat and go straight for the nearest living human.

Central Narrative: What is speculated to be its first victim was a woodworker specializing in custom statues. It's believed that the vulture killed the victim as opposed to feasting on their corpse.

Ever since the first body was found, mutilated and dismembered, many more bodies soon popped up with similar disfigurements. This caused many problems for local law enforcement.

The Foundation stepped in when a video of the creature was brought into the hands of the police. What caught their eye was the unnatural material it seemed to be made out of.

The Foundation easily caught it with the scent of human flesh, but they did not fully understand its eating habits at the time, nor did they anticipate the consequences of the lack of understanding that they had. They tried to feed it animal carcasses. They were able to keep it for 2 days before it escaped in one of its “frenzy states” and ate a facility guard alive. It was soon recaptured and given human flesh to eat. It hasn't escaped, nor tried to escape since then.

Presently, the SCP sits in its containment cell, docile. It is given a pound of human flesh every 24 hours. It seems to be satiated.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The simple but unique appearance and description combined with the grotesque nature of its feeding.

Additional Notes: “How's The Foundation able to obtain the human flesh that they feed the SCP?”

The Foundation has struck a deal with a nearby city using one of their front companies, which allows them access to unwanted or unclaimed dead bodies. They also have access to the corpses of people who have donated their bodies to science.

I’d be willing to delete the “escaped and ate a guard” part to make The Foundation not look like idiots.

If this ever gets greenlit I’d like to include a brief cross-link to SCP-3847 if possible.

item.title: SCP Concept: Life is short
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A humanoid SCP that is given birth to by a randomly picked woman in labour across the world, however the SCP will only live for 24 hours and when it dies another woman gives birth to it. It varies gender between times.

Central Narrative: A woman is in a hospital, going through labour, and finally gives birth to her child. She's happy, but something feels off, the child doesn't scream and both her and the doctors are shocked and panicked, until the baby speaks to them and wiggles itself free. When on the ground, it introduces itself to them before being taken to a special room in the hospital. The child doesn't understand them and tries to leave the room before being studied by doctors, amongst them an undercover Field Agent from the Foundation. It soon explains itself to the team and it's able to escape from the hospital. After that it seeks new places to go, observe, study and learn. This SCP was then reported to the Foundation and later was observed and studied a few times by the Staff.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The most interesting thing about this anomaly is that the SCP can remember past life experiences, it can grow very intelligent and wise over years and aqquire knowledge for many things, even as a newborn, and it's believed that it's main purpose is to learn. The only limits it has is it's very short life and it's physical form when both very young and very old. The SCP is also never born with any defficiency. What's also interesting about this SCP is that currently it poses no threats to humans, however, as it grows more intelligent there is a possibility of it attempting to end humans.

Additional Notes: Some of the SCP's origin was discovered in a few interviews the Foundation had with it, it was discovered who it's first birth mother was and when it was created. The SCP also explains it's theory in how and why this anomaly was made and how it is yet to discover how to stop it. The anomaly is normally calm during interviews and shows no interest in harm of any life form, however it is triggered when reminded it has a short life cycle.

item.title: An Empty Cell (Looking for Greenlights)
item.description: An unused containment cell that makes people think there is an SCP in it, with a twist
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Thought to be an unused containment cell that makes everyone who is aware of it think that an SCP is contained inside. This effect only works once per person and can be canceled out by simply stepping inside of SCP-XXXX. Although the affected individuals are all convinced that an SCP exists within SCP-XXXX, none of them can recall any details of the SCP. Due to its effects providing little to no risk to the safety of personnel working at the site, all new members transferred there are to be exposed to SCP-XXXX's effects and then going inside of SCP-XXXX, preventing the effect from repeating in that individual.

Show Narrative
Hide Narrative

Central Narrative: All of the above is stated in the description. Which is contained in an expandable block reading archived, and followed by "Further testing must be done to determine the nature of SCP-XXXX due to Incident-Placeholder." Incident-Placeholder details a newly transferred researcher being exposed to SCP-XXXX and following the procedures, stepping inside to remove its effects, however, this time he didn't come out. The stationed guards were sent inside to discover his corpse lying dead on the floor of SCP-XXXX. They also noted a note on the entrance of SCP-XXXX, noting, "I warned you, you didn't listen." This is followed by an addendum describing emails of a researcher requesting permission to conduct tests on SCP-XXXX, in order to prove her theory.

Her theory claims that there is in fact an SCP inside of SCP-XXXX, an SCP that has the ability to alter or block the formation of memories of anyone that is aware of it to not include it, and it is likely that whoever brought this SCP in has already lost all memories of how they did it, containing it in an anomalous cell just before all their memories were gone as a last-ditch effort in containing it.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think people will be hooked and read further on to find out what the SCP is.

Additional Notes: The incident is not named placeholder, it is a placeholder for when I come up with a name. This isn't above 400 words, I just checked.

(I am now aware of 055, but I think the main thing is based around SCP-XXXX and not what it is containing, so it could still work.)

item.title: The Copy - Idea
item.description: I like to write and draw. Got bored so I thought why not?
item.content:encoded:
Nickname: "The Copy".
Class: Safe Euclid

I've always had an interest in writing and I've have been writing for a couple years now, on an app called Wattpad. My writing has flaws but bare with me please. And let me know if an idea like it has already been used, I'd hate to feel as if someone already had the idea and I was taking it.

"Copy" is a very strange female humanoid with charcoal coloured skin around the head and neck. The rest fades into very pale and normal skin. It's hair is pure white and it has no recognizable facial features, even when direct light is on it's face. It's movements are slow but, despite it's lack of eyes, seems to know exactly where it is going.

Copy was found standing on a bridge near an extremely old forest. It made no effort to run or even hide from personnel. However, once they were close enough, It slowly pointed to a particularly dark clearing in the distance of the forest. Upon investigating, a body of a female was found wearing the exact same clothes as Copy (a stripped shirt falling off her shoulders and a light grey, 2 tier skirt). The body's skull had been removed but the rest of the body was still there. The identity of the corpse couldn't be discovered but it's killer was nearby and terminted. It was apprehended and brought in for questioning. However, to question it, you need to spend longer than necessary with it, as explained below.

The most unique thing about Copy is the way it manages to speak. While it cannot speak on it's own terms, it can mimic another person's facial features (including skin) and voice. The face is copied while it's hair and the rest of it's body remains the same. To answer the Foundation's questions, she will copy the face and words said to her in the exact tone and pitch of the person in front of her. This lead to quite a bit of irritation when talking to it, unless you are not easily angered, as the foundation had no idea how to get answers out of it. Than all of a sudden it spoke back, answering as many questions as it could with the words it's interviewer spoke. The way it spoke back is by using the words spoken to her, just chopped up (think of video game modders, occasionally they have to cut up NPC dialogue to make voices), to make legible sentences. The issue is that once the interviewer has stopped talking to it, it removes any source of conversation it previously had with the interviewer, so no matter how long the foundation spoke with Copy, she would always forget. And if too many people are speaking at once, she will manage to form all faces on it's face and overlap all the words speaking.

On quite a few occasions, 073 was the one to be sent to question it, due to his genuine friendliness and calm personality. 073
spent 3 hours speaking to Copy and had quite a few questions answered. I imagine it like this:

073: Hello
Copy: Hello
073: How are you?
Copy: How are you?
073: Are you…Copying me?
Copy: Are you…Copying me?
073: Okay…What's your name?
Copy: Copy. What's your name?
073: Cain, or 073, if you prefer
Copy: Cain
073: Yes, that's my name
Copy: How are you?

Or something like that. I imagine if you talk enough than it is more than happy to talk back.

It isn't at all aggressive towards personnel and quite passive about aggressive things that are said to it. It's interesting to watch people insult it for the insult to bounce back at them.

I set it to Euclid because when a breach occurs, she flips out, destroying her containment cell and anyone who enters while this is happening. So far, I'd imagine only a small amount of lives cover her hands, so when she appears agitated, just leave her be until she literally knocks herself out.

item.description: A Lost Prince with an unworldly handsomeness looking for his home until the SCP Foundation Found Him
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Speech: SCP- XXXX is a young man that has an unnatural hair and eye color that changes depending on his mood, with a short height, an unnatural pale skin and mostly of all, has an unworldly charisma. He wears a crown and clothes of a prince like those in fairytales indicating that he's from another world or the era where royals exists (I'm still looking for what that era or time was called). SCP-XXXX shows no sign of aging and has an ungodly regenaration ability but most of all his presence makes people love him romantically despite their gender, but being expose to XXXX longer makes them more love him and more exposure can make people be obsessed with him and makes people fight to death for his love and for more longer exposure, it can make them crazy and insane, deeming themselves not worthy of XXXX's love and commits suicide, though the worst part is the dead body of the people that surrounds XXXX turned to smoke which XXXX absorbs enhancing his regenerative ability.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX was found wandering around the forest of one of the facilities of the SCP Foundation with confusion and sadness written on his face and hair that keeps turning to yellow and blue. The personnels that was guarding the perimeter of the said facility, find it weird and interesting at the same time, and without hesitation quickly implemented an order to quickly capture him.

They quickly send out a team to capture him, though upon contact the agents stopped and examine XXXX intently. XXXX quickly introduced himself with a smile as Prince Jun, his hair and eye color turning in a bright yellow, the agents dropped their weapons, going on their knees and bows towards him.

Meanwhile, The researchers that was watching from the CCTV cameras find it odd and interesting, and continued to watch what would happen. And from the footage they saw that all of the agents are kissing XXXX hands before they quickly stand up and leads him towards the SCP Facility, but before they can reach the gates all the agents started to act weird, first it started by bickering, to arguing, but the last is the most unexpected as the agents out of nowhere started killing each other while XXXX just continue to walk towards the gates without batting an eye.

item.title: Modern Day Soldier
item.description: has exceptional skills in hand-to-hand combat and use of modern day weaponry
item.content:encoded:
First SCP idea. An entity that takes the form of a soldier. This soldier has exceptional skills in hand-to-hand combat and use of modern day weaponry.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes!

Page Type: SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch: My SCP idea is an entity that takes a form of a soldier (pretty much a U.S Soldier).

  • Has a unique form that make him invulnerable to most damage (mainly being bullets, his form weakens by any sort of explosives)
  • Has weapons that are connected to him and cannot be removed (if someone attempts to, the soldier gets irritated and even aggressive)
  • The soldier entity gets PTSD an effect that resembles PTSD, while in this state, he goes berserk, destroying everything he sees in a fit of rage.
  • Can communicate with humans in mainly English
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: This SCP is an unknown entity that takes the form of a soldier. No one knows exactly what the entity is or why it's taking the form of a soldier, but theories are that the entity was released from an unknown containment in an anonymous operation led by the U.S Government. This SCP is an excellent hand-to-hand fighter, shooter, and uses military strategies. This SCP is also known to be relatively peaceful (as it is a soldier), but can be violent if angered, or in the state of his PTSD effect. The U.S Government insists that they know nothing of the soldier, but some scientists think they are lying. SCP officials think that the soldier was once a leader of the squad with how he talks and uses his strategies of moving through buildings/locations and how secretive he is in interviews. The form of this SCP is unknown to SCP officials as it's an unusual substance and can make the wearer immune to most damage. This SCP is known to get out of containment easily when angered by officials or D-Class, but seems blind when in it's PTSD effect.

Hook/Attention-Grabbers: I find this idea for an SCP to be unique because you don't see a lot of humanoid SCPs with actual guns. I find that what's best about SCPs is the mystery around them; like where they come from and what the goals of the SCPs are. This idea has a bit of mystery of who the soldier is, what the form substance could be, and I will probably add more mysteries to this SCP if I am able to write about it.

The overall concepts that I think makes this idea unique: An SCP who uses modern day weapons to dispatch enemies, the mystery of this SCP, and that it's a soldier SCP.

Additional Notes: NONE.

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous snow globe that contains a fully functional society of individuals who have been transported into it. The victims of the globe are almost instantaneously erased from all historical records and human memory.

Central Narrative: In December, 2019, a low level foundation member purchased a snow globe from a Christmas shop to gift his significant other. It caught his eye because of the realistic landscape of the snow globe, but when the gift was opened a half a month later, there were certain features that had appeared on the landscape that the foundation member were not there when he purchased the globe, such as a crop field and a few crude houses. The foundation personnel brought the globe to the foundation and has since been on 24-hour observation by a camera which has documented the progress of the internal civilization.

+ show block
– hide block

While on an expedition/hunting an SCP/recovering from a containment breach, a foundation team reported the immediate disappearance of a team member, as if he had been swallowed up by the air in front of him. As foundation command began to question the team on the specifics of the disappearance immediately following the incident, they could not recall the existence of the team member at all, and foundation records of the team suggested likewise. The identification of a disappearance was nonetheless recorded. The anomalous properties of the snow globe were only discovered when the camera observing the snow globe recorded a flare gun fire from within the forest of the globe approximately 3 minutes after the disappearance of the team member. Currently no attempts have been made from the inhabitants of the interior to communicate with the foundation, and it is unknown whether the victims are aware of their situation. When foundation personnel revisited the site of the disappearance, nothing occurred, and the source of victimization remains unknown.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: While the idea of a miniature self-contained civilization isn’t completely unique, the events that resulted in the discovery of the anomaly is testament to the aptitude of the foundation. Someone had to be curious enough, or the foundation is thorough enough, that the cross reference between the report of the disappearance and the observation of the flare within the globe was able to occur. Regardless, it was a fun and engaging idea to develop.

Additional Notes: I’m open to ideas on making the civilization itself more engaging, but I think the disconnect between the inhabitants of the globe and the foundation is interesting on its own. I’m also considering including a label that says SCP Foundation, which would allude that the globe might be a failed experiment and/or one from another reality.

item.title: Ideas for execution of a "Monster What Kills You" skip
item.description: I like a challenge.
item.content:encoded:
At some point in the near future (perhaps after the posting of one or more other articles) I would really like to take on the writing challenge of making a "classic monster" skip interesting. It's such a commonly-avoided topic that I can't help but be enticed to try and make it work. Here are some qualities such a hypothetical monster would have to include, as part of the challenge:

  • Very little in the way of motivation, i.e. a predator or something similar
  • Irrepressibly violent tendencies towards humans, i.e. this is just a thing what kills you
  • No cop-outs or deceptions as to its nature, i.e. it is exactly what it seems to be.

Given these constraints, the most plausible avenue to success seems to be setting the monster within a narrative that stands on its own. However, even that feels like cheating to me, as by shifting the focus of the article from the monster to the story, I've effectively conceded that it is simply impossible to make a monster interesting nowadays.

Does anyone know of some modern skips that could provide inspiration? Do you have any ideas about what would be necessary to make this challenge possible? Do you believe it is possible at all? Should I abort this ill-conceived venture at once??? Please let me know.

If it goes well, I might try to do the same for an x-man.

SCP-XXXX has an appearance that of a faucet from manufacturer "Delta Faucets". SCP-XXXX can function similarly to a usual faucet, with the exception that the water by SCP-XXXX usually has a discharge rate of 61.6 μL/s, whether supplied with water or not. If so that SCP-XXXX is not supplied with water, the drops will be more purplish per 17 minutes of use. SCP-XXXX is sentient this is confirmed as SCP-XXXX can communicate in Morse, discovered after a level 4 researcher, who was fluent in Morse, noticed that the drops discharged by SCP-XXXX took in the order of
…. .. / .- (- -.) (.-) (..) (-.) (- -..- -) / -.. .-. .-.-.-, to which translate to "hi again, dr.".

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX can also create music with its drops, as such to the range from note C1 to F7. Led to an incident of it playing SCP-407.

A simpler description of this would be the fact that SCP-XXXX separates the waveform of the human voice when entered upon an oscillator. Pitches made by SCP-XXXX, when combined, make a waveform that someone would identify as a recording of someone's voice seemingly in his 40's, talking to someone he calls "Aleph". When questioned about who "Aleph" is, SCP-XXXX stated that "Aleph" was actually the level 4 researcher. Said researcher was notified of this recording and proceeded to interview SCP-XXXX for further questioning.

SCP-XXXX once distributed information kept hidden by the O5, how it knew that information is currently unknown.

Central Narrative:
The article has interviews with SCP-XXXX, some in Morse Code, and a visualized explanation of the exceedingly complex form of communication used by SCP-XXXX. Will be in ACS, classified safe,
disruption class Vlam (due to the SCP-407 incident), Risk class Critical (also of SCP-407).

Hook/Attention Grabber:
As much as it is sentient, SCP-XXXX shows a fair degree of omniscience. Morse code known by SCP-XXXX is international, but also fluent in American Morse. The extremely complex communication is basically:

  • Get some waves
  • Translate it to drops
  • Get those waves and combine them
  • Get an oscillator and combine them
  • Play the combined wave

SCP-XXXX has no recollection of how it knows O5 information.

Additional Notes:
I actually got this idea while in the shower. I stood just in front of the faucet and was mesmerized by how the drops falling resembled music. It gave me an idea, however.

item.title: Twisting Termite Tunnels
item.description: Seems like the little buggers can get into anything...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Not yet, I suppose…?

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-Fi, Nature Documentary, Comedy(?)

Elevator Pitch: Termites with a nest-building behavior that can bypass conventional spatial limitations, including covering immense distances and moving in and out of perfectly sealed spaces. Pretty much the same goals, needs, and individual intelligence of ordinary termites in all other respects.

Central Narrative: The first clue is the identification of Australian compass termites somewhere that they definitely should not be. Further investigation leads to exploration of their tunnels and the discovery that distant places are connected through seemingly-random twists and turns, which the insects have no trouble navigating but are confusing to a human sense of direction. There's a conspicuous lack of pocket dimensions, thaumaturgical Ways, or significant gravitational anomalies involved, at least as far as the Foundation can initially detect.

The Foundation would be up against mundane technological limitations on what sort of equipment can fit down an individual termite tunnel, as any substantial damage to the structures promptly collapses their anomalous effects.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: We have an otherwise mostly mundane (if highly industrious) social insect species that cannot be reliably confined to a single habitat, although it's not an immediate Veil risk unless people start trying to identify individual termite species. What's more, they've created a functional hyperspace network out of nothing but soil and their own feces - and wouldn't the Foundation just love to learn how that works?

Additional Notes: Researching mundane eusocial insects is still relatively cutting-edge science, since they tend to live underground and it's hard to study large-scale emergent behaviors outside their natural habitat. I intend to research more into the kinds of technology used for these purposes, and play with how the Foundation might take them further. I could see this having a lot of experiment logs - perhaps taking reader suggestions, if the article were to take off.

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: A dark web page that lists the names of many different people, ranked from 1 to 100. Each name is accompanied by a price, and the names change almost daily. Anyone who views the site will always end up on the list and disappear sometime in the future.

Central Narrative: A recent suicide in urban California has a man dead at his computer, a note at his side, and a bullet through his head. The paper talks of the Indigo Branch, and how to get to it on the dark web. It also talks about how the man had received a steady amount of cryptocurrency over the past few months, and with his life in a bad situation, began using the money in an effort to turn everything around. The sender quickly begins talking to him, and says they will continue giving him money as long as he uses his coding knowledge to help locate information on the people whose names appear on the site. He soon stops helping the anonymous sender, and finds his name in the seventh spot on the list within a few days. He decided to kill himself rather than face the online criminals for his mistake.

+ show block
– hide block

An interested Foundation personnel looks deeper into this case, and starts using the site to track down the people he sees high up on the list. He finds that they all disappear at seemingly random times, some only hours after being on the list, and others who never disappeared before the personnel went missing himself. Because of the bizarre way these people go missing - seeming to vanish out of thin air most times - the Indigo Branch was categorized as an anomaly, and is only viewable by those with higher clearance.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Instead of another entity that just rips your face off for looking at it, or a spooky room that turns you into a chair, the Indigo Branch is just a single web page with names and numbers, who change at random intervals and correspond to real people. Less than being horrifying, this SCP is mysterious, allowing the reader to interpret everything in their own way.

Additional Notes: My biggest concern here is if I mistakenly wrote something that has already been written and solidified as an SCP. There are so many out there, and I have only read a few here and there, that is is a distinct possibility it may already exist. If this is the case, please let me know!
